question: The relation between electric energy, power and time is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Energy = Power × Time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **electric energy**, **power**, and **time** is given by the equation: **Energy (E) = Power (P) × Time (T)**. This is the correct and universally accepted formula.
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which energy is transferred or converted. It is measured in **watts (W)**, where 1 watt = 1 joule per second (J/s).
 
• **Energy** is the total amount of work done or the total power consumed over a period of time. It is measured in **joules (J)** in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• **Time** refers to the duration for which the power is being consumed or transferred. It is measured in **seconds (s)**.
 
• For practical applications, energy is often measured in units like **kilowatt-hours (kWh)** when dealing with electrical energy consumption. For example, energy consumed by household appliances is calculated in kWh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Units:**

 
 
• **Power (P)**: Measured in **watts (W)**, it represents the rate of energy consumption or production.
 
• **Energy (E)**: Measured in **joules (J)**, it represents the total energy consumed or produced. For electricity billing, it is measured in **kilowatt-hours (kWh)**, where 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
 
• **Time (T)**: Measured in **seconds (s)** or hours (h), it refers to the duration of power usage.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• The formula **E = P × T** is used in calculating the energy consumption of electrical devices. For example, a 100 W bulb running for 10 hours consumes 1 kWh of energy (100 W × 10 h = 1000 Wh = 1 kWh).
 
• It is also used in industries to determine the energy efficiency of machines and devices.
 
 
 
• **Common Misconceptions:**
 
 
• The incorrect statement "Energy = Power + Time" violates the dimensional consistency of the formula, as power and time are measured in different units and cannot be added directly.
 
• Similarly, "Energy = Power / Time" is incorrect because dividing power by time does not yield energy.
 
• "Energy = Time - Power" is also incorrect, as subtraction of time and power is not mathematically or physically meaningful.
 
 
 
• **Additional Insights:**
 
 
• In mechanical systems, a similar relationship exists: **Work = Force × Distance**. This highlights the universality of the concept of energy transfer.
 
• Modern electricity meters calculate energy consumption in terms of **kWh**, which is a direct application of the formula **E = P × T**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SI Units:**

 
 
• **Power**: 1 watt (W) = 1 joule/second (J/s).
 
• **Energy**: 1 joule (J) = 1 watt-second (W·s).
 
• **Time**: Measured in seconds (s) for scientific calculations and hours (h) for practical purposes.
 
 
 
• **Energy Billing:** Energy consumed by households is typically billed in **kilowatt-hours (kWh)**, a practical unit of electrical energy.
 
• **Examples of Power and Energy:**
 
 
• A 60 W lightbulb used for 5 hours consumes 0.3 kWh of energy.
 
• An electric heater rated at 2000 W running for 2 hours consumes 4 kWh of energy.
